input.strategy_title: Surface model deployment status in the RHOAI Dashboard
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists deploying models through the Dashboard cannot tell whether a
deployment is healthy without leaving the console. InferenceService state is
only visible via `oc get inferenceservice` or by reading Kubernetes events,
which most Dashboard users cannot access. Support cases regularly begin with
"my model has been Pending for an hour" — information the platform already has
but does not surface.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users see a deployment status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for each deployed model in the Dashboard model serving views. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Users can open a status detail view showing the underlying condition messages and recent events for a failed or progressing deployment. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Displayed status reflects the actual InferenceService state within 30 seconds of a change, without a manual page reload. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Users can filter and sort the deployed models list by status. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation explains each status value and the first troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe

## Out of Scope

- Alerting or notifications on status transitions
- Status history / timeline views
- ModelMesh deployments (KServe InferenceService only)

## Open Questions

None blocking — KServe already exposes the needed conditions on the
InferenceService status; this strategy is about surfacing them.

# Surface KServe InferenceService deployment status in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers user-visible deployment status for KServe InferenceService
models in the RHOAI Dashboard model serving views. Data scientists will see a
status value (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for each deployed model directly in
the console and can drill into a status detail view showing the underlying
condition messages and recent events. This removes the
need to leave the Dashboard and inspect InferenceService state with `oc` or
raw Kubernetes events. Automatic status refresh (30-second freshness) and
status-based filtering/sorting of the list are delivered as separately
planned capabilities that build on this epic.

## Scope

- Derive a three-value deployment status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for each
  deployed KServe InferenceService from its CR status conditions (e.g. Ready,
  PredictorReady) as exposed by the `serving.kserve.io/v1beta1` InferenceService
  CRD. The Dashboard reads the CRs through the Kubernetes API; no KServe code
  changes are required — the conditions are consumed as-is.
- Display the derived status for each deployed model in the Dashboard model
  serving views (deployed models list).
- Add a status detail view that, for a failed or progressing deployment, shows
  the underlying InferenceService condition messages and recent Kubernetes
  events.
- Out of scope: alerting/notifications on status transitions, status history /
  timeline views, and ModelMesh deployments (KServe InferenceService only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a deployed model whose InferenceService is ready, when the user opens
  the Dashboard model serving view, then the model is shown with status
  "Ready".
- Given a model whose InferenceService reports non-ready conditions, when the
  user opens the model serving view, then the model is shown with status
  "Progressing" or "Failed" as appropriate to its conditions.
- Given a failed or progressing deployment, when the user opens the status
  detail view, then the underlying InferenceService condition messages and
  recent Kubernetes events for that deployment are displayed.
- Status derivation is validated against real InferenceService CR status
  conditions: the three displayed values are derived from conditions the
  InferenceService already exposes (passive KServe component — no KServe code
  changes; the Dashboard consumes the existing CR status and events).
- Status is surfaced only for KServe InferenceService deployments; ModelMesh
  deployments are not affected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): status display for each deployed model in model serving views —
  covered by the status column and derivation logic.
- HLR-2 (P0): status detail view with condition messages and recent events —
  covered by the detail view scope.

# Document deployment status values and Failed-deployment troubleshooting

## Description

This epic delivers product documentation for the new Dashboard model
deployment status capability. It explains what each status value (Ready,
Progressing, Failed) means for a deployed model and gives users the first
troubleshooting steps to take when a deployment is Failed, so they can resolve
common issues without opening a support case.

## Scope

- Author a new documentation topic (or section within the existing model
  serving documentation) covering the deployment status feature in the
  Dashboard model serving views.
- Explain each status value — Ready, Progressing, Failed — including how each
  relates to the underlying InferenceService state.
- Document the status detail view: what condition messages and recent events
  show and how to read them.
- Provide first troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments (e.g. opening the
  status detail view and reading the condition messages and events).
- Describe filtering and sorting the deployed models list by status.
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process and tooling for authoring and
  publishing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains each deployment status value (Ready, Progressing,
  Failed) shown in the Dashboard model serving views.
- Documentation includes the first troubleshooting steps for a Failed
  deployment, referencing the status detail view and its condition messages /
  events.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented Dashboard status
  behavior (statuses, detail view, filtering/sorting) before publication.
- Content is validated for accuracy against the architecture context for the
  Dashboard and KServe (status is derived from InferenceService CR status
  conditions; ModelMesh deployments are not covered).
- Documentation states scope accurately: no alerting/notifications, no status
  history/timeline, KServe InferenceService only.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2): product documentation explains each status value and first
  troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments — fully covered by this epic.

# Keep Dashboard deployment status current within 30 seconds without manual reload

## Description

This epic delivers automatic freshness for the deployment status surfaced in
the RHOAI Dashboard model serving views. Once a KServe InferenceService
changes state, the displayed status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) reflects the
new state within 30 seconds, without the user reloading the page. It builds
on the status display and the status retrieval path for deployed models
delivered by the core deployment-status work: it keeps that already-displayed
data current and cannot be built before the status display and its data
retrieval exist. Deliberately split out so freshness can be planned and, if
needed, deferred independently of the P0 status display (status shown on page
load remains useful without it, and adding refresh later requires no rework).

## Scope

- Keep the displayed deployment status for each deployed KServe
  InferenceService current: a change in the actual InferenceService state is
  reflected in the Dashboard within 30 seconds, without a manual page reload.
- Choose and implement the refresh mechanism (polling vs. Kubernetes watch) —
  an implementation decision for the Dashboard team; either mechanism is
  acceptable as long as the 30-second bound holds.
- Out of scope: alerting/notifications on status transitions, status history /
  timeline views, and ModelMesh deployments (KServe InferenceService only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a change in the actual InferenceService state (e.g. a deployment
  transitions from Progressing to Ready), when the user is viewing the model
  serving page without interacting with it, then the displayed status
  reflects the new state within 30 seconds without a manual page reload.
- Given the refresh mechanism chosen (polling or watch), when the Dashboard
  model serving views are open, then the displayed status data is at most 30
  seconds stale relative to the actual InferenceService state.
- Freshness behavior applies only to KServe InferenceService deployments;
  ModelMesh deployments are not affected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): displayed status reflects the actual InferenceService state
  within 30 seconds of a change, without a manual page reload — covered by
  the refresh scope.

# Add status filtering and sorting to the deployed models list

## Description

This epic delivers list controls on the Dashboard deployed models list so
users can narrow and order deployments by their status value (Ready,
Progressing, Failed). It builds on the deployed models list and its status
column delivered by the core deployment-status work: the controls operate on
status data that is already displayed. Deliberately split out so the list
controls can be planned and, if needed, deferred independently of the P0
status display (the status column ships and is useful without list controls,
and adding the controls later requires no rework).

## Scope

- Add a status filter control on the deployed models list: selecting a status
  value (Ready, Progressing, Failed) shows only models whose deployments have
  that status.
- Add a status sort control on the deployed models list: the list can be
  ordered by status value.
- Out of scope: alerting/notifications on status transitions, status history /
  timeline views, and ModelMesh deployments (KServe InferenceService only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the deployed models list showing models with mixed statuses, when the
  user filters by status "Failed", then the list shows only models whose
  deployments are Failed.
- Given the deployed models list, when the user sorts by status, then the list
  is ordered by the selected status ordering.
- Given no status filter is selected, when the user views the deployed models
  list, then all deployed models are shown (filtering is opt-in and does not
  hide rows by default).
- Filtering and sorting apply only to KServe InferenceService deployments;
  ModelMesh deployments are not affected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): users can filter and sort the deployed models list by status —
  covered by the list controls scope.

Surface model deployment status in the RHOAI Dashboard.
